business_model.basis: stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business description
business_model.claim: Victoria's Secret & Co. is a specialty retailer of women's intimates, apparel, and beauty products sold under the Victoria's Secret, PINK, and Adore Me brand names to female consumers worldwide.
quotes: Victoria's Secret & Co. (together with its subsidiaries unless the context otherwise requires, "we", "us", "our" or the "Company") is a specialty retailer of women's intimates and other apparel and beauty products marketed under the Victoria's Secret, PINK and Adore Me brand names.

business_model.claim: The company operates as a single reporting segment that serves customers worldwide through stores and digital channels.
quotes: We operate as a single segment designed to seamlessly serve customers worldwide through stores and digital channels.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 MD&A
business_model.claim: In fiscal 2025, net sales of $6.553 billion were split across three channels: North American stores at $3.544 billion (54%), digital at $2.042 billion (31%), and international at $967 million (15%).
quotes: The North American stores channel represents our physical retail locations in North America and accounted for $3.544 billion, or 54%, of our net sales in 2025.
The digital channel accounted for $2.042 billion, or 31%, of our net sales in 2025.
International net sales accounted for $967 million, or 15%, of our net sales in 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in the 8-K earnings release and 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: In Q2 2026, net sales of $1,610.7 million grew 10% year-over-year, driven by 9% growth in North American stores, 8% growth in the direct channel, and 20% growth internationally, with total comparable sales up 9%.
quotes: Net Sales Increased 10% to $1.611 Billion, Near High-End of Guidance
Total comparable sales for the second quarter of 2026 increased 9%.
In North America, net sales increased 9% in the stores channel and increased 8% in the direct channel compared to the second quarter of 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 1 Business – Seasonal Business
business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal, with two principal selling seasons (Spring in Q1–Q2 and Fall in Q3–Q4); the fourth quarter, including the holiday season, typically accounts for approximately one-third of net sales and is normally the most profitable quarter.
quotes: Our operations are seasonal in nature and consist of two principal selling seasons: Spring (the first and second quarters) and Fall (the third and fourth quarters). The fourth quarter, including the holiday season, typically accounts for approximately one-third of our net sales and is normally our most profitable quarter.

business_model.claim: The company evaluates net sales through five drivers: traffic, conversion, units per transaction, average unit retail, and average transaction value.
quotes: To evaluate our net sales, we utilize traffic, conversion (which we define as the percentage of customers who visit our stores or digital sites and make a purchase), units per transaction, average unit retail (which we define as the average price per unit purchased) and average transaction value (which we define as units per transaction multiplied by average unit retail).

business_model.basis: F2 provides the GAAP figures; P4 MD&A explains the tariff refund component
business_model.claim: Costs of goods sold, buying, and occupancy was $852 million in Q2 2026 on net sales of $1,611 million, yielding a gross profit of $759 million (47.1% gross margin), though this was inflated by a $135 million IEEPA tariff refund recorded as a reduction of COGS.
quotes: we recorded $140 million of pre-tax income in the 2026 Consolidated Statements of Income, which included $135 million as a reduction of costs of goods sold, net of related costs and other items

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Risk Factors and 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: Tariffs imposed by the U.S. government in 2025 negatively impacted operating income by approximately $85 million (net of mitigation efforts), and the company is still navigating new tariff regimes under Section 122 and Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 in 2026.
quotes: We estimate tariffs, net of mitigation efforts, negatively impacted our operating income during fiscal 2025 by approximately $85 million and resulted in increased expenses, supply chain disruption, and uncertainty.
In July 2026, the U.S. administration imposed new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, effective July 24, 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 1 – Merchandise Vendors and Product Design, Development and Sourcing
business_model.claim: The company purchased merchandise from approximately 335 vendors in 2025, the largest of which accounted for approximately 13% of purchases by spend, with a globally distributed sourcing base in the U.S. and Southeast Asia.
quotes: During 2025, we purchased merchandise from approximately 335 vendors located throughout the world, the largest of which accounted for approximately 13% of our purchases by spend.
We have cultivated a strong sourcing presence in the U.S. and Southeast Asia, helping to drive innovation and speed-to-market across our product categories.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 1 – Franchise, License and Wholesale Arrangements
business_model.claim: International revenue is generated through a partner-based model: 562 partner-operated stores in approximately 70 countries (franchise, license, wholesale), a China joint venture with 65 stores, and company-owned digital sites; royalty rates are generally low-double digits to low-teens as a percentage of partner sales.
quotes: Additionally, we have more than 560 stores in approximately 70 countries operating under franchise, license and wholesale arrangements.
Royalty rates, which are generally low-double digits to low-teens, vary based on store format, local business conditions and various other factors.

business_model.basis: F2 provides the GAAP line items; P4 MD&A explains the drivers
business_model.claim: In Q2 2026, general, administrative, and store operating expenses were $502 million, up from $478 million in Q2 2025, while operating income (before the tariff refund) was boosted by improved merchandise margins and higher sales volume.
quotes: The increase in operating income compared to the second quarter of 2025 was primarily driven by an increase in net sales, a $135 million benefit from the recognition of IEEPA tariff refund recoveries in costs of goods sold and improved merchandise margins.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K Item 1 and Item 7, and reiterated in Q2 2026 10-Q and earnings release
business_model.claim: The company's 'Path to Potential' growth strategy is built on four priorities: supercharging bra authority, recommitting to PINK, fueling growth in beauty, and evolving brand projection and go-to-market strategy.
quotes: Our growth plan, which we call "Path to Potential," is built around four key priorities: supercharging our bra authority, recommitting to PINK, fueling growth in beauty and evolving our brand projection and go-to-market strategy.

Our two iconic brands, Victoria's Secret and PINK, have a strong global presence and high awareness among consumers. Their combined market share in the intimates category remains strong, underscoring our leading position in the industry and providing a significant competitive advantage.

competitive_position.claim: The company operates two market-leading intimate apparel brands (Victoria's Secret and PINK), an industry-leading beauty business, and a digitally-native brand (Adore Me/DailyLook).

risks.claim: Heavy seasonal concentration in the fourth quarter means a soft holiday season could disproportionately reduce full-year profitability.
quotes: The fourth quarter, including the holiday season, typically accounts for approximately one-third of our net sales and is normally our most profitable quarter.

We experience major seasonal fluctuations in our net sales and operating income, with a significant portion of our operating income typically realized during the fourth quarter holiday season. Any decrease in sales or margins during this period could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, non-GAAP reconciliation footnotes a and c). The figures are reported GAAP charges.
risks.claim: The Adore Me acquisition has generated significant impairment and restructuring charges, raising questions about the integration's value creation.
quotes: In 2025, we recognized pre-tax expense of $120 million ($90 million after-tax) … related to the impairment of certain Adore Me long-lived tangible and intangible assets.

In 2025, we recognized a pre-tax charge of $36 million ($28 million after-tax) … related to inventory reserves and severance expense as a result of unique operational disruptions that led to the restructuring of our Adore Me and DailyLook fulfillment operations.

risks.basis: Stated in P7 (8-K Item 5.02, filed October 12, 2026). The departure date and transition terms are contractual as described in the filing.
risks.claim: The departure of Chief Legal and Compliance Officer Melinda McAfee (effective March 31, 2027) creates a leadership gap in a period of elevated regulatory and trade-policy complexity.
quotes: Melinda McAfee, Chief Legal and Compliance Officer, will be leaving the Company, effective March 31, 2027. The Company has initiated a search for a successor.

Ms. McAfee will retain her current role until a successor Chief Legal Officer has been appointed, and during such period, she will be entitled to receive the same compensation and benefits as are currently in effect.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated directly in P4 (10-Q MD&A, Tariffs and Macro Environment section) as unclear
unresolved_questions.claim: The financial impact of the new Section 301 tariffs (10% to 12.5%, effective July 24, 2026) on the company's future results of operations is not yet known
quotes: In July 2026, the U.S. administration imposed new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, effective July 24, 2026. It is unclear at this time what impact tariffs will have on our future results of operations, including any changes in tariff levels or the imposition of new tariffs or other trade policies.

P4.s21.text: Net sales in the second quarter of 2026 increased 10%, to $1.611 billion, compared to the second quarter of 2025.

P6.s29.text: The Company is now forecasting fiscal year 2026 net sales to be in the range of $7.100 billion to $7.180 billion, an increase compared to the previously communicated guidance range of $7.030 billion to $7.130 billion, and compared to net sales of $6.553 billion in fiscal year 2025.
